/-!
# The implicit graph conjecture

The implicit graph conjecture (Kannan–Naor–Rudich question, Spinrad's conjecture) asserts that
every hereditary family of graphs of at most factorial speed of growth admits an efficient
implicit representation, i.e. an adjacency labeling scheme with $O(\log n)$-bit labels.
It was refuted by Hatami and Hatami (FOCS 2022), who constructed, for every $\delta > 0$,
a hereditary family of at most factorial speed whose implicit representations need labels of
length $\Omega(n^{1/2 - \delta})$. Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems still
records the conjecture as open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Implicit graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/implicit_graph_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics]
  (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [KNR92] S. Kannan, M. Naor, S. Rudich, *Implicit representation of graphs*,
  SIAM J. Discrete Math. 5 (1992), 596–603.
- [Sp03] J. P. Spinrad, *Efficient Graph Representations*, Fields Institute Monographs 19,
  AMS (2003).
- [HaHa22] H. Hatami, P. Hatami, *The Implicit Graph Conjecture is False*, FOCS 2022,
  [arXiv:2111.13198](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.13198).
-/

blocks.code: abbrev GraphFamily : Type := ∀ n : ℕ, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))
blocks.docstring:
A family of finite labelled graphs: `F n` is the set of members of the family whose vertex
set is `Fin n`, i.e. the $n$-vertex graphs of the family, following [HaHa22].

justification.closest_existing_considered: A plain `Set (Σ n, SimpleGraph (Fin n))` or `Set (SimpleGraph V)` for a fixed V; neither captures the per-n counting |F_n| conveniently.
justification.name: ImplicitGraphConjecture.GraphFamily
justification.why_needed: Type of families of labelled finite graphs indexed by vertex count, `∀ n, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))`, matching the F_n of the sources.

blocks.name: GraphFamily
blocks.text:
/-- A family of finite labelled graphs: `F n` is the set of members of the family whose vertex
set is `Fin n`, i.e. the $n$-vertex graphs of the family, following [HaHa22]. -/
abbrev GraphFamily : Type := ∀ n : ℕ, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))

blocks.code:
def IsHereditary (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃m n : ℕ⦄, ∀ G ∈ F n, ∀ H : SimpleGraph (Fin m), H ⊴ G → H ∈ F m
blocks.docstring:
A graph family is *hereditary* if it is closed under taking induced subgraphs: whenever
`G ∈ F n` and `H` is a graph on `Fin m` isomorphic to an induced subgraph of `G`, then
`H ∈ F m`. Taking `m = n` shows that a hereditary family is closed under isomorphism.
Equivalently, the family is defined by a (possibly infinite) set of forbidden induced
subgraphs.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `SimpleGraph.IsIndContained` (`⊴`), which is used inside the definition; `SimpleGraph.Embedding`/`SimpleGraph.comap`.
justification.name: ImplicitGraphConjecture.IsHereditary
justification.why_needed: Closure of a graph family under induced subgraphs (forbidden-induced-subgraph characterisation); no such predicate on families exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.

blocks.name: IsHereditary
blocks.text:
/-- A graph family is *hereditary* if it is closed under taking induced subgraphs: whenever
`G ∈ F n` and `H` is a graph on `Fin m` isomorphic to an induced subgraph of `G`, then
`H ∈ F m`. Taking `m = n` shows that a hereditary family is closed under isomorphism.
Equivalently, the family is defined by a (possibly infinite) set of forbidden induced
subgraphs. -/
def IsHereditary (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃m n : ℕ⦄, ∀ G ∈ F n, ∀ H : SimpleGraph (Fin m), H ⊴ G → H ∈ F m

blocks.code:
def HasAtMostFactorialSpeed (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, ((F n).ncard : ℝ) ≤ 2 ^ (C * n * Real.log n)
blocks.docstring:
A graph family has *at most factorial speed of growth* if the number of $n$-vertex members
is at most $2^{O(n \log n)}$, i.e. there is a constant $C$ with $|F_n| \le 2^{C n \log n}$
for all $n$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Asymptotics.IsBigO` applied to `fun n => Real.log (F n).ncard`; an explicit constant was preferred for readability.
justification.name: ImplicitGraphConjecture.HasAtMostFactorialSpeed
justification.why_needed: The growth condition |F_n| ≤ 2^{O(n log n)} for a graph family; not in Mathlib.

blocks.name: HasAtMostFactorialSpeed
blocks.text:
/-- A graph family has *at most factorial speed of growth* if the number of $n$-vertex members
is at most $2^{O(n \log n)}$, i.e. there is a constant $C$ with $|F_n| \le 2^{C n \log n}$
for all $n$. -/
def HasAtMostFactorialSpeed (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, ((F n).ncard : ℝ) ≤ 2 ^ (C * n * Real.log n)

blocks.code:
def HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  ∃ (C : ℝ) (D : List Bool → List Bool → Bool), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G ∈ F n,
    ∃ ℓ : Fin n → List Bool,
      (∀ v, ((ℓ v).length : ℝ) ≤ C * Real.log n) ∧
        ∀ u v, G.Adj u v ↔ D (ℓ u) (ℓ v) = true
blocks.docstring:
A graph family has an *efficient implicit representation* (an *adjacency labeling scheme*
with $O(\log n)$-bit labels) if there are a constant $C$ and a *decoder*
`D : {0,1}* × {0,1}* → Bool`, both depending only on the family, such that every $n$-vertex
member `G` of the family admits a labeling of its vertices by binary strings of length at most
$C \log n$ from which adjacency is recovered by the decoder: `G.Adj u v ↔ D (ℓ u) (ℓ v)`.

Following [HaHa22], no computability or running time requirement is imposed on the decoder.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None; `SimpleGraph.Embedding` into a graph on labels was considered but is the universal-graph formulation instead.
justification.name: ImplicitGraphConjecture.HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation
justification.why_needed: Adjacency labeling scheme with O(log n)-bit labels and a family-level decoder; no notion of implicit representation / labeling scheme exists in Mathlib or the repo.

blocks.name: HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation
blocks.text:
/-- A graph family has an *efficient implicit representation* (an *adjacency labeling scheme*
with $O(\log n)$-bit labels) if there are a constant $C$ and a *decoder*
`D : {0,1}* × {0,1}* → Bool`, both depending only on the family, such that every $n$-vertex
member `G` of the family admits a labeling of its vertices by binary strings of length at most
$C \log n$ from which adjacency is recovered by the decoder: `G.Adj u v ↔ D (ℓ u) (ℓ v)`.

Following [HaHa22], no computability or running time requirement is imposed on the decoder. -/
def HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  ∃ (C : ℝ) (D : List Bool → List Bool → Bool), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G ∈ F n,
    ∃ ℓ : Fin n → List Bool,
      (∀ v, ((ℓ v).length : ℝ) ≤ C * Real.log n) ∧
        ∀ u v, G.Adj u v ↔ D (ℓ u) (ℓ v) = true

blocks.code:
def HasPolynomialUniversalGraphs (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ U : SimpleGraph (Fin (n ^ C)), ∀ G ∈ F n, G ⊴ U
blocks.docstring:
A graph family has *induced-universal graphs of polynomial size* if there is a constant $C$
such that for every $n$ there is a graph $U_n$ on $n^C$ vertices containing every $n$-vertex
member of the family as an induced subgraph.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `SimpleGraph.IsIndContained` (used inside); no universal-graph notion exists in Mathlib.
justification.name: ImplicitGraphConjecture.HasPolynomialUniversalGraphs
justification.why_needed: Induced-universal graphs of size n^{O(1)}, the standard equivalent formulation (used for the variant theorem).

blocks.name: HasPolynomialUniversalGraphs
blocks.text:
/-- A graph family has *induced-universal graphs of polynomial size* if there is a constant $C$
such that for every $n$ there is a graph $U_n$ on $n^C$ vertices containing every $n$-vertex
member of the family as an induced subgraph. -/
def HasPolynomialUniversalGraphs (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ U : SimpleGraph (Fin (n ^ C)), ∀ G ∈ F n, G ⊴ U

    answer(False) ↔ ∀ F : GraphFamily, IsHereditary F → HasAtMostFactorialSpeed F →
      HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation F := by

blocks.docstring:
**The implicit graph conjecture** ([KNR92], [Sp03]; see also [HaHa22, Conjecture 1.1]).

Is it true that every hereditary graph family with at most factorial speed of growth (at most
$2^{O(n \log n)}$ labelled $n$-vertex members) has an efficient implicit representation, i.e.
an adjacency labeling scheme with labels of $O(\log n)$ bits?

Kannan, Naor and Rudich posed this as a question and Spinrad stated it as a conjecture.
The answer is **no**: Hatami and Hatami [HaHa22] proved that for every $\delta > 0$ there is a
hereditary graph family of at most factorial speed every implicit representation of which
requires labels of length $\Omega(n^{1/2 - \delta})$.

blocks.docstring:
**The implicit graph conjecture**, formulated with induced-universal graphs.

Is it true that every hereditary graph family with at most factorial speed of growth has
induced-universal graphs of polynomial size $n^{O(1)}$?

A family has an efficient implicit representation if and only if it has induced-universal graphs
of polynomial size [KNR92], so this is equivalent to `implicit_graph_conjecture` and its answer
is also **no** [HaHa22].

claims.decomposer_note: Precise form (Kannan–Naor–Rudich question, Spinrad's conjecture; Hatami–Hatami arXiv:2111.13198 Conj. 1.1): every hereditary graph family F (closed under induced subgraphs / isomorphism, i.e. having a forbidden-induced-subgraph characterization) with at most factorial speed of growth (|F_n| ≤ 2^{O(n log n)} labeled n-vertex graphs) admits an efficient implicit representation, i.e. there are C and a decoder D : {0,1}* × {0,1}* → Bool depending only on F such that every n-vertex G ∈ F has a vertex labeling by ≤ C·log n bits with adjacency = D(label u, label v); equivalently F has induced-universal graphs of polynomial size n^{O(1)}. Subtleties: the decoder need not be computable (Hatami–Hatami drop the poly-time requirement, and their lower bound holds regardless); the quantifier order is ∃ constant/decoder for the whole family, then ∀ graphs; the statement is a single Prop whose answer is False — refuted by Hatami–Hatami (FOCS 2022: for every δ>0 there is a factorial hereditary family needing codes of length Ω(n^{1/2−δ})) — so despite the list's 'open' status it should be recorded as research solved with answer(False).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful proposition (Hatami–Hatami Conj. 1.1 form: ∀ hereditary F of at most factorial speed, ∃ constant C and decoder D (uniform for the family, no computability), ∀ n, ∀ G ∈ F n, ∃ O(log n)-bit labels decoding adjacency), recorded as research solved with answer(False). c04 chosen as base: hereditary via Mathlib's `⊴` (IsIndContained, equivalent to comap along Fin m ↪ Fin n and closed under isomorphism at m = n), real uniform constants for speed (|F_n| ≤ 2^{C n log n}) and label length (≤ C log n), Bool decoder, complete docstrings and references, proven `test` lemmas for each bespoke definition, plus the faithful equivalent induced-universal-graph variant (∃ C, ∀ n, ∃ U on n^C vertices with every G ∈ F n ⊴ U), which is the form in which Hatami–Hatami actually prove the lower bound. Boundary cases checked: n = 0,1 satisfy the speed bound trivially (≤ 1 labeled graph, 2^0 = 1); n = 1 forces empty labels which is harmless; u = v included in the adjacency equivalence only forces decoder irreflexivity on used labels (equivalent up to constant factor); exactly n^C universal-graph vertices is equivalent to ≤ n^C by padding with isolated vertices. My edits: wrapped three >100-char lines and added a sentence noting the Wikipedia list's stale 'open' status.

context: In the study of graph algorithms, an implicit graph representation (or more simply implicit graph) is a graph whose vertices or edges are not represented as explicit objects in a computer's memory, but rather are determined algorithmically from some other input, for example a computable function.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single-slot decomposition and its precise formulation (hereditary + factorial speed ⟹ O(log n)-bit adjacency labeling scheme; decoder not required to be computable; research solved with answer(False)) agree with Hatami–Hatami Conjecture 1.1 and the Wikipedia article.

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem hasEfficientImplicitRepresentation_bot :
    HasEfficientImplicitRepresentation fun _ => {⊥} := by
  refine ⟨0, fun _ _ => false, fun n G hG => ⟨fun _ => [], fun v => by simp, ?_⟩⟩
  simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hG
  subst hG
  simp

/-- The family of edgeless graphs has induced-universal graphs of polynomial size. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem hasPolynomialUniversalGraphs_bot : HasPolynomialUniversalGraphs fun _ => {⊥} := by
  refine ⟨1, fun n => ⟨⊥, fun G hG => ?_⟩⟩
  simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hG
  subst hG
  exact ⟨⟨(finCongr (Nat.pow_one n).symm).toEmbedding, by simp⟩⟩

end ImplicitGraphConjecture

items: Recorded as `research solved` with `answer(False) ↔ P` (as the decomposition notes instruct), rather than `¬ P`: Kannan–Naor–Rudich posed it as a question and Spinrad restated it as a conjecture; Hatami–Hatami (FOCS 2022) refuted it.
Graph family modelled as `F : ∀ n : ℕ, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))`, i.e. F n is the set of labelled n-vertex members with vertex set Fin n, exactly as in Hatami–Hatami's setup (F_n = graphs on [n]).

Hereditary is defined via Mathlib's induced containment `H ⊴ G` (`SimpleGraph.IsIndContained`, existence of a graph embedding, which is injective and preserves and reflects adjacency). This is literally Hatami–Hatami's definition (for every injection σ:[m]→[n] and G ∈ F_n, G.comap σ ∈ F_m), and includes closure under isomorphism (m = n).

Factorial speed is `∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n, |F n| ≤ 2^(C * n * log n)` with `∀ n` rather than 'eventually': equivalent, because each F n is finite (SimpleGraph (Fin n) is a finite type) so finitely many exceptions can be absorbed into C, and n = 0, 1 hold trivially (at most one graph, and 2^0 = 1). `Set.ncard` is used; it is exact here since F n is always finite.

Label length bound is `(ℓ v).length ≤ C * Real.log n` with a real constant C (natural log; base only changes C). Labels are binary strings `List Bool` of length at most C log n (the notes' '≤ C·log n bits'); Hatami–Hatami's exactly-w(n)-bit codes are equivalent up to a constant via self-delimiting padding. At n = 1 this forces the empty label, which is harmless: the single 1-vertex graph only needs D([],[]) = false.

Adjacency condition is required for all ordered pairs `∀ u v` (including u = v, forcing D(a,a) = false on used labels). This matches the induced-universal-graph formulation (embeddings are injective and universal graphs are loopless) and is equivalent to the u ≠ v version up to a constant factor in label length (append a vertex index).

Following Hatami–Hatami, the decoder is an arbitrary function `List Bool → List Bool → Bool` with no computability/polynomial-time requirement (the original KNR definition requires poly-time decoding). Dropping it weakens the conjecture, and the refutation holds regardless, so `answer(False)` is correct for both readings.

Added an equivalent variant `implicit_graph_conjecture.variants.universal_graphs` using induced-universal graphs of polynomial size (`∃ C : ℕ, ∀ n, ∃ U : SimpleGraph (Fin (n ^ C)), ∀ G ∈ F n, G ⊴ U`), since Wikipedia and the notes emphasise this equivalent formulation (KNR92). Exactly n^C vertices is equivalent to at most n^C by padding with isolated vertices; n = 0 with C ≥ 1 gives the empty universal graph, into which the empty graph embeds. Hatami–Hatami's lower bound is proved via universal graphs, so this variant is also refuted.
Five small `category test` lemmas with complete proofs exercise the definitions on the family of all graphs and the family of edgeless graphs.

reviewer_notes: The list entry is a bare title; the precise statement was taken from the Wikipedia 'Implicit graph' article and Hatami–Hatami arXiv:2111.13198 (Conj. 1.1, Thm 1.2), whose definitions (labeled families F_n on [n], hereditary = closure under induced subgraphs along injections, at most factorial speed = |F_n| ≤ 2^{O(n log n)}, decoder not required computable) the final file follows exactly. Status: Wikipedia's list still says 'open', but the conjecture was refuted (FOCS 2022), so the file uses `research solved` with `answer(False) ↔ …` (the repository idiom for a question answered negatively, used e.g. in WrittenOnTheWallII and Wikipedia/Fuglede). Differences among candidates were only cosmetic/equivalent: Nat.log vs Real.log vs n^(Cn) vs big-O for the speed bound; 'for all n' vs 'eventually'; Bool vs Prop decoder; whether u ≠ v is assumed in the adjacency equivalence; c01 additionally required injective labels (a harmless strengthening equivalent up to constants, but not in the source definition, so not preferred). No candidate omitted the slot and no omission reasons needed weighing. The extra variant `implicit_graph_conjecture.variants.universal_graphs` is included because both Wikipedia and the decomposition notes present polynomial-size induced-universal graphs as the equivalent formulation and Hatami–Hatami's refutation is stated in that language. Final file compiles with only `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
